title: Language Names and Tokens with Text

blocks.text: A Program Variable and a Name in the Text

The string "crea balance=8;balance+2;" is data for our interpreter. Compiling C++ does not automatically declare a variable named balance from those characters. First, we must recognize names, a declaration keyword, and the = sign. Later, we will build the place where their values are stored and the statements that create them.

Our name starts with an ASCII letter A..Z or a..z. It continues with letters, digits, or _. It contains from one to twelve characters. Case matters. The exact word crea is reserved; crea2 and Crea are names. This is a rule of the interpreted language, narrower than the general rules for C++ identifiers.

blocks.question: Which is an allowed name under this contract?
blocks.explanation: The name must begin with a letter. Underscores and digits are allowed after the first character.

blocks.text: A Category with the Appropriate Data

Token now retains clase, valor, and texto. A number uses valor and leaves texto empty. A name uses texto and leaves valor as zero. Signs, the word crea, and the end marker leave both extra fields empty: a zero and an empty string. Every field is initialized; the reader checks that consistency before reserving a token.

The constants numero, nombre, declaracion, and final_texto identify internal categories. Their char values do not dictate which input letters are allowed. Input containing the letter f is now recognized as a name, not as the end marker; only exhaustion of the stream produces the end category.

blocks.text: Read Up to the End of the Name

Extracting a string with >> would read balance+2; as a single word if there were no spaces. Our lexer accumulates only name characters. It returns the first successfully read delimiter so it remains available to the next call. If the stream ends exactly after the name, the lexer returns that name without attempting to put back a nonexistent character.

Therefore balance+2; yields a name, +, a number, ;, and the end marker. The reserved word is compared only when the entire name is available: crea2 cannot be split into crea followed by 2. A thirteenth character rejects the name; discarding an operation was introduced earlier so the interpreter can continue after its ;.

blocks.question: The stream reaches its end just after the word Box. What should the lexer do?
options: Put back the last character even though the final read failed.
Invent a semicolon to complete the operation.
Return Name: Box; the following read returns the end marker.
blocks.explanation: EOF ends the name but does not complete a statement that requires ;. No character is put back after a failed read.

blocks.text: A Worked Inspection Before Interpretation

This program only inspects tokens. The word crea and = are recognized, but we do not yet execute a declaration or give balance a value. Reading characters and accepting a statement are different responsibilities.

The buffer holds only one token. token_valido must accept the new categories with their appropriate data; extending the lexer without extending this check would break the connection between modules. Separators remain spaces, tabs, and newlines; prepared text contains up to 120 characters.
Compare Delimiters and Complete Words

blocks.question: Predict the inspector's lines for a word resembling the reserved one and a name containing an underscore.
answers:
Name: crea2
Sign: =
Number: 7
Sign: ;
Name: A_3
End
blocks.explanation: crea2 is a complete name. A_3 ends when the source is exhausted; that end does not supply a ;.

blocks.question: Write only the string member operation that checks whether a sign's text field is empty.
blocks.explanation: empty checks whether the string is empty. A zero numeric value alone does not verify the text field.

blocks.text: Guided Integration: Check the Extended Buffer

Rebuild the reader and lexer shown earlier; integrate tokens with text and write a client for "Hallway_2*4;". Read the first name, return it, obtain it again, and continue inspecting the rest. The buffer preserves both the category and the text. Display Reserved: Hallway_2, then Sign: *, Number: 4, Sign: ;, and End, one line for each unit.

Also test "n;", "Crea;", "crea;", "A1_B;", "abcdefghijkl;", "abcdefghijklm;", and "_A;". The letter n does not become a number just because it matches an internal label. Twelve characters are accepted and thirteen are rejected. A name at the end is delivered before End.

Criteria: the complete token data survive reservation, the keyword is recognized only on a complete match, delimiters are preserved, the name length limit is enforced, and a character is not put back after a failed read. Returning another token to an already full buffer must be rejected without losing the reserved one.
Reference for the Follow-Up Check

The reference uses different names and signs but retains the same interface. It neither reserves two tokens nor copies the reader: istringstream is not copyable. The next stage will associate names with persistent values.

Name-bearing tokens are discussed in the supporting source (Stroustrup, 2024, sections 6.6.1 and 6.8.2, and exercise 1 of chapter 6). The ASCII name grammar, the word crea, and the practice cases are original.
